mechanism.observer_cfg: Entire new module is under cfg(test) in the Unix-only module. ProcessHandle attachment and snapshot methods are cfg(all(test, unix)).
statistics: bytes whose existing channel send returned error
last read result including zero-byte EOF, successful count, raw errno or error without OS errno
terminal read-loop error, distinct from an earlier transient WouldBlock
mechanism.descriptor_queries: F_GETFL and FIONREAD only. No read, poll wait, write, termios update, readiness clear, duplication, or descriptor close.
mechanism.association: Each existing PtyIo creates its own observer. The reader and ProcessHandle share only Arc<observer>; observer stores Weak<AsyncFd<File>>, never a cached raw integer fd or long-lived strong fd reference.
mechanism.snapshot_lifetime: Weak upgrade temporarily pins the same already-owned AsyncFd during two non-consuming syscalls. The temporary Arc is dropped at the end of that match arm; no descriptor is retained by the returned String or observer. If upgrade fails, descriptor_released is reported.
mechanism.timing: The only print is immediately after the original timeout result and existing exit-state print, before the existing side-channel read/terminate block. It cannot change the already-returned timeout result. The sample is after that decision, not an atomic historical snapshot at the deadline.
mechanism.errors: F_GETFL/FIONREAD errors retain their raw errno as Err rather than being converted to zero. Task-handle poison and missing handles remain explicit.
mechanism.atomic_limit: Independent relaxed atomic samples are observations, not an atomic protocol state or admission conditions. The raw read-result tag+value itself occupies one AtomicU64. No diagnostic value drives I/O or test pass/fail.
mechanism.statistics_api: One named ReaderEvent/observe entry point; no single-call setter methods.

non_test_behavior.pty_rs: Only cfg(all(test, unix)) attachments/getters are added; the ordinary spawn/handles/waiter/terminator path is unchanged.
non_test_behavior.process_rs: Only cfg(all(test, unix)) observer field/init and methods are added; ordinary fields and lifecycle methods remain unchanged.
non_test_behavior.unix_io_rs: No observer exists outside tests. The AsyncFd Arc gets an equivalent local binding; the real read result gets an equivalent local binding before return. EOF/error arms still break, Interrupted still continues, one unchanged send occurs after each positive read, the writer is untouched.

throughput_source_findings: PtyIo::new duplicates and registers AsyncFd exactly once per PTY session, before spawn tasks; the read loop does not create AsyncFd or kqueue registrations.
The read task creates one 8192-byte stack buffer outside its loop and reuses it.

Each positive read still copies a Vec and makes the original bounded mpsc send. A closed receiver produces a send error but the loop continues. This candidate neither optimizes nor bypasses that behavior.

These facts do not prove the actual Intel cause. The new per-read observation adds unit-test-only atomic operations, and may itself perturb scheduling; successful or failing future evidence must preserve that scope.

bazel_registration.source_rule: defs.bzl:319 lib_srcs = crate_srcs or native.glob(["src/**/*.rs"], exclude = binaries.values(), allow_empty = True)

qualification.configured_mac_and_main_hosts: root observed both arm64; no native Intel inference from those hosts
qualification.original_31_roster: must remain exactly unchanged on the original macOS Intel target

scope_exclusions: No production I/O repair is claimed.
No altered read batch, new raw-mode setting, timeout extension, additional timer, retry, skip or assertion relaxation.
No native/shared worktree/ref/CI mutation was performed by the author.
The original failing log and prior collector-only history remain immutable.

version_history.reason: independent review identified single-call small setters contrary to AGENTS; replaced with explicit ReaderEvent + one observe method, preserving observation semantics
